binding_record_note: Two type records, four public fields and seventeen callable compiler records. Two additional CXXConstructor records are excluded by the inventory as template-owned declarations; their visible FunctionTemplate records are bound once.
changes: Real repr(C) nodes own native key/value payloads, a real inherited hash-chain prefix and independent nonowning order pointers.
All three set constructor families and all data copy/move/in-place families are represented; construction copies item before key and destruction destroys key before item.
Public native order fields are exposed as typed read/mutable-pointer projections, with stored pointers independent of payload type to retain Rust covariance.
Allocation precedes constructor callbacks; constructor failure and native deletion release the matching typed allocation.
Shared NativeNodeOwner and map_payload retain existing unwind cleanup; no duplicated allocator ownership implementation.
BasicMapNode/BasicMapNodeMut drive actual ordered traversal, with set keys read-only.
Ten scalar/aligned native layouts and allocator spans match pinned x86_64 GCC; native header hashes verified against compiled include tree.
trait_evidence: Set/data node payload lifetimes and both owner aliases are covariant.
Heap owner types remain Unpin with PhantomPinned payloads; standalone pinned payload nodes remain !Unpin.
Raw-link node/owner Send and Sync restrictions are retained; no blanket unsafe thread impls added.
limitations: OrderedMap/OrderedDataMap still allocate prior OrderedTable slot nodes; these newly ported real node classes are not yet the map engine. Next batch must replace that representation with these actual nodes and canonical links.
Node layout evidence is concrete x86_64 GCC cases, not a universal C++ ABI or ZST equivalence proof.
Custom C++ move hooks are represented by Rust ownership transfers; generic conversion and caller-observable moved-from behavior remain boundary work.
Native noexcept destruction terminates on throwing destructors; Rust panic cleanup tests are explicit safety extensions, not native exception-behavior parity.
Allocation/copy/drop phase probes do not certify constructor callbacks inspecting partially initialized node bytes.
Inherited ListNode/TListNode methods use the existing project implementations; this batch adds node-specific projections, not a fresh full inherited API denominator proof.
Scoped checks and bindings do not replace main whole-workspace or full API/test parity certification.
